title: Low-degree Fourier weight bound
statement: Let $n,k$ be nonnegative integers, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ take only the values $0$ and $1$, and suppose its uniform mean is $\alpha$, where $0<\alpha\le 1$. If $k\le \frac{373}{1000}\log(1/\alpha)$, then the sum of the squares of the Fourier coefficients of $f$ over subsets of at most $k$ coordinates is at most $\alpha^{21/20}$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
